# **1\. Requirements**

State what the system must do and the important quality or timing constraints. Requirements should be specific, testable, and traceable to the proposed design (you may add more FR and/or NFR as needed).

## **1.1 Functional Requirements**

| ID | Requirement | Task Allocation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR1 | The system shall publish telemetry (motion, sensor, and event data) over MQTT to the broker. | Buddy 1 |
| FR2 | The system shall receive and act on remote commands (e.g. car/cmd/start) via MQTT subscription. | Buddy 1 |
| FR3 | The system shall automatically recover WiFi/MQTT connectivity after a network drop, using backoff and reconnection. | Buddy 1 |
| FR4 | The motion control subsystem shall provide reusable functions for forward movement, backward movement, left turn, right turn, u-turn, and stop, each callable independently by other subsystems. | Buddy 2 |
| FR5 | The motion control subsystem shall dynamically correct differences between left and right wheel speed during straight-line travel, using a closed-loop PID controller running on encoder feedback.  | Buddy 2 |
| FR6 | The motion control subsystem shall calculate the vehicle's speed (cm/s) and cumulative distance travelled (cm) using wheel encoder pulse counts, updated at a fixed interval no slower than 50 ms.  | Buddy 2 |
| FR7 | The system shall detect and decode directional barcodes accurately while the vehicle is moving at varying speeds. | Buddy 3 |
| FR8 | The car shall follow the track line using IR sensor feedback to maintain center-line tracking. | Buddy 3 |
| FR9 | The car shall detect and decode Code 39 directional barcode symbols and map decoded characters to navigation commands (A \= left, B \= right, C \= straight, D \= u-turn). | Buddy 3 |
| FR10 | The system shall detect complete track loss and initiate line reacquisition. | Buddy 3 |
| FR11 | The system shall detect speed humps from IMU pitch/acceleration data, estimate hump height from pitch and encoder distance, and log/report the highest hump peak experienced during the run. | Buddy 4 |
| FR12 | The system shall detect collision events using IMU data(Buddy 4\) and command the motion-control subsystem to stop the vehicle(Buddy 2). | Buddy 4 / Buddy 2 |
| FR13 | The system shall support a controlled handoff between obstacle-avoidance manoeuvres and line reacquisition. | Buddy 3 / Buddy 5 |
| FR14 | The system shall detect obstacles via a two-stage ultrasonic process (coarse scan followed by a fine scan) to determine obstacle location, width, and a bypass direction with safe side clearance. | Buddy 5 |

## **1.2 Non-Functional Requirements**

| ID | Requirement | Task Allocation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR1 | MQTT publishing shall be non-blocking; telemetry shall be buffered or dropped on link loss rather than stalling the main control loop. | Buddy 1 |
| NFR2 | Wheel encoder pulses shall be captured using GPIO interrupts on both wheels independently, with zero missed counts under normal operating speed (target: up to 50 cm/s).  | Buddy 2 |
| NFR3 | The PID controller shall keep a 1 m straight-line run at nominal cruise speed within ±5 cm of lateral drift. | Buddy 2 |
| NFR4 | Motion commands shall achieve distance accuracy within \+/- 3% of commanded distance and turning accuracy within \+/- 5 degrees of commanded angle. | Buddy 2 |
| NFR5 | The motion-control codebase shall be packaged as a modular, standalone C library to support clean integration with the rest of the system. | Buddy 2 |
| NFR6 | The motion subsystem shall expose speed, distance travelled, and encoder counts through a defined read-only API, refreshed at the same interval as FR6, for consumption by the communication layer. | Buddy 2 |
| NFR7 | IR sensors shall be sampled at a fixed 5 ms period (within the 5–10 ms target band) to hold center-line tracking. | Buddy 3 |
| NFR8 | A decoded barcode shall be validated according to the defined barcode format before the associated navigation command is executed. | Buddy 3 |
| NFR9  | Barcode decoding shall classify narrow and wide elements by their ratio to the median element width, using encoder velocity to convert edge timing into distance, so decoding works across the full operating speed range. | Buddy 3 |
| NFR10 | On receiving a collision signal, the vehicle shall come to a full stop within 200 ms, measured from the IMU spike to zero encoder speed. | Buddy 4 / Buddy 2 |
| NFR11 | Hump detection shall detect at least 95% of humps in test runs, and the reported peak height shall be within ±20% (or ±0.5 cm, whichever is larger) of the physically measured height. | Buddy 4 |
| NFR12 | IMU motion classification shall raise no false collision events and misclassify no more than 5% of motion events (accelerating, cruising, turning, hump) over the standard test runs. | Buddy 4 |
| NFR13 | If IMU Processing does not refresh its IMU\_ALIVE heartbeat within 50 ms, the Safety task shall stop the vehicle and latch a fault. | Buddy 4 / Buddy 2 |
| NFR14 | The obstacle avoidance sequence, including leaving the line, bypassing the obstacle, and reacquiring the original line, shall be completed within 3.0 s (Week 10 grade-A target) and shall never exceed 5.0 s. | Buddy 5 |
| NFR15 | Ultrasonic measurements shall be filtered (median of 3 pings per bearing) before obstacle profiling, keeping obstacle width estimation error within 10%. | Buddy 5 |
| NFR16 | The system software shall run on the micro T-Kernel RTOS, be implemented in C using the Pico C SDK, and conform to the Barr C Coding Standard: public functions carry a module prefix (motion\_, lf\_, bc\_, obs\_, imu\_, safety\_, vc\_, tel\_), types use the \_t suffix, and fixed-width integer types from \<stdint.h\> are used throughout. | Everyone |
| NFR17 | Every inter-task queue shall have a defined depth, send timeout and receive timeout (Section 3.3); no task at priority 1–7 shall block on a queue whose consumer runs at a lower priority. | Everyone |

# **3\. RTOS Task Table**

List the proposed RTOS tasks. Priorities are preliminary at Week 6 and must be justified. 

| Task | Purpose | Inputs | Outputs | Trigger | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Safety / Collision Response | Force immediate motor stop on collision | COLLISION and IMU\_ALIVE flags from IMU Processing (EVF\_SAFETY) | motion\_emergency\_brake() call; FAULT\_LATCHED flag; fault event to Telemetry | Event-driven: tk\_wai\_flg with 50 ms timeout (IMU watchdog) | 1 |
| Vehicle Controller  | Resolve competing navigation commands into one command for Motion Control | MBF\_NAV\_IN: steering (Line-Following), nav command (Barcode Decode), bypass and RELEASE (Obstacle Avoidance), remote start/stop/reset (Telemetry); FAULT\_LATCHED | Single resolved motion command to Motion Control; status events to Telemetry; clears FAULT\_LATCHED on reset | Event-driven (tk\_rcv\_mbf on MBF\_NAV\_IN) | 2 |
| Motion Control (PID)  | Drive motor PWM; execute move/turn/u-turn/stop from the resolved command  | Encoder counts (from ISR); resolved command (MBF\_MOTION\_CMD, polled each tick); FAULT\_LATCHED | Motor PWM (M1A/B, M2A/B); motion\_state\_t (speed, distance, counts) | Periodic, 20 ms | 3 |
| Line-Following Control  | Maintain center-line tracking  | IR\_L, IR\_C (ADC)  | Steering correction to Vehicle Controller every 20 ms; LINE\_FOUND flag | Periodic, 5 ms | 4 |
| Barcode Decode  | Capture & decode Code 39 symbols  | IR\_BC edge timestamps (ISR ring buffer); vehicle velocity from motion\_state\_t | Decoded nav command (A/B/C/D) to Vehicle Controller | Event-driven (woken by GP28 ISR) | 5 |
| Obstacle Scanning  | Sweep servo, acquire filtered range  | Ultrasonic echo, servo position  | Obstacle profile (bearing, width, clearance) to Obstacle Avoidance | Periodic, one servo step per 60 ms; fine scan on detection | 6 |
| Obstacle Avoidance & Recovery  | Choose bypass direction; hand off to line-following  | Obstacle profile; LINE\_FOUND flag | Bypass commands and RELEASE to Vehicle Controller; AVOID\_ACTIVE / LINE\_REACQUIRED flags | Event-driven (obstacle profile received) | 7 |
| IMU Processing  | Filter IMU data; compute pitch/roll; classify motion; detect humps & collisions  | Raw accel/gyro  | Hump events; COLLISION and IMU\_ALIVE flags; motion state | Periodic, 10 ms | 8 |
| Telemetry / MQTT  | Publish telemetry; parse remote commands; monitor the connection | Sensor/state data, MQTT messages  | car/telemetry/\* and heartbeat topics; parsed remote commands to Vehicle Controller | Periodic 200 ms \+ event-driven (MQTT receive) | 9 |

## **3.1 Ownership and Justification Table** {#3.1-ownership-and-justification-table}

| Task | Owner | Justification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Safety / Collision Response  | Buddy 4 (detection, watchdog) / Buddy 2 (brake function) | A detected collision must override every motion or navigation command and force an immediate stop, so this task preempts everything. It never waits indefinitely: it waits on COLLISION with a 50 ms timeout and stops the car if IMU Processing has not refreshed IMU\_ALIVE in that time. This bounds the risk of the collision detector itself running at a low priority (P8). |
| Vehicle Controller  | Buddy 2 | Line-Following, Barcode Decode, and Obstacle Avoidance can all issue a command to Motion Control in the same cycle. Without one arbitration point, two subsystems could send conflicting motion commands on the same tick and Motion Control has no rule for which one wins. This task is the single place that decides, and it also holds the authority mode (LINE or AVOID) used for the avoidance handoff. |
| Motion Control (PID)  | Buddy 2  | The control loop must run at a fixed periodic rate to hold stable wheel speed correction. Missing even one tick under CPU load causes the PID controller to over-correct or drift, so it needs to preempt perception and comms work, but it must never override the safety stop above it.  |
| Line-Following Control  | Buddy 3  | The vehicle drifts off the track within a few hundred milliseconds if this loop is delayed, since IR sampling must hold a 5 ms period (NFR7). It sits directly below Motion Control: the PID loop it feeds must never miss a tick, but line tracking outranks all perception and communication work. |
| Barcode Decode  | Buddy 3  | Edge timestamps are captured in the GP28 interrupt, so edges are not lost when this task is delayed. The task only has to drain the 64-entry edge buffer before it fills (one symbol is 29 elements) and deliver the command before the junction, so it sits directly below Line-Following. |
| Obstacle Scanning  | Buddy 5  | Scanning doesn't need per-tick precision like line tracking, but it must complete a scan cycle before the vehicle reaches an obstacle at operating speed. It preempts background work (IMU, telemetry) but doesn't need to compete with the core navigation loop.  |
| Obstacle Avoidance & Recovery  | Buddy 5 (bypass logic) / Buddy 3 (line reacquisition handoff)  | Directly below Obstacle Scanning, because it consumes scan data and only runs after a detection. The handoff back to line-following must still be prompt, or the vehicle keeps drifting off its intended path. |
| IMU Processing  | Buddy 4  | The filter and classification pipeline tolerates more jitter than the closed-loop control tasks, since hump and pitch data feed a report rather than an actuator. Collision detection also runs here, so it is protected by the Safety task’s 50 ms IMU\_ALIVE watchdog, and its worst-case detection latency will be measured against NFR10 (A7). |
| Telemetry / MQTT  | Buddy 1  | Per NFR1, publishing must stay non-blocking, so it can’t compete with control tasks for real hardware urgency, but it still needs regular execution so telemetry to the operator dashboard doesn’t go stale. Connection monitoring (heartbeat, keep-alive, backoff) runs inside this task rather than in a separate one. |

## **3.2 Timing Constants and Initial Thresholds**

| Parameter | Initial value | Used by / notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Line-Following sample period | 5 ms | Line-Following (NFR7) |
| Steering post interval | 20 ms | Line-Following → Vehicle Controller; aligned with the PID loop |
| Motion Control period | 20 ms | Motion Control (FR6) |
| IMU sample period | 10 ms | IMU Processing |
| IMU watchdog | 50 ms | Safety stops the car if IMU\_ALIVE is not refreshed (NFR16) This is Safety's timer, not IMU Processing's. Safety expects IMU Processing to "check in" (refresh a heartbeat flag) at least once every 50ms. If that check-in doesn't happen, either because IMU Processing crashed, stalled, or the I2C bus hung, Safety assumes the worst and stops the car anyway, even though no actual collision was detected. This is what makes the collision response trustworthy even though the detector itself only runs at low priority (P8). |
| Telemetry publish / heartbeat | 200 ms / 1 s | Telemetry / MQTT (FR1) |
| Servo step (coarse sweep) | 60 ms per step; 5 bearings, 30° apart | Obstacle Scanning The ultrasonic sensor sits on a servo that sweeps side to side. Instead of sweeping smoothly, it stops at 5 fixed angles, pausing 60ms at each to take a reading. |
| N (hysteresis) | 3 samples (15 ms) | Junction and line-lost detection The sensor reading has to agree 3 times in a row before the car believes it. One flickery reading (dust, a shadow, a seam in the tape) doesn't count. This exists so the car doesn't twitch or falsely declare a junction because of a single noisy sample. |
| T\_lost | 100 ms | Line-Following: both sensors light While driving normally, if both line sensors read “no line” continuously for 100ms, the car gives up and says "I've lost the line," entering LINE\_LOST. This is the timer for the ordinary case: cruising along and the line just isn't under the sensors anymore. |
| T\_turn | 500 ms | Line-Following: line must reappear after a turn This one only starts counting after the car executes a barcode turn command. It's a longer grace period (500ms vs. 100ms) because right after a turn, it's normal and expected for the line to be briefly out of sensor range while the car swings around. T\_turn is patience specifically for "I just turned, give the line a moment to reappear" before also declaring LINE\_LOST. |
| T\_uturn | 1.0s | Line-Following: line must reappear after a u-turn A u-turn pivots the car 180° in place, which takes about twice as long as a 90° turn, so the line stays out of sensor range for longer. T\_uturn replaces T\_turn only after a U-turn command, giving the car that extra time before it declares LINE\_LOST. |
| T\_search | 2.0 s | Line-Following: reacquisition search before TRACK\_LOST Once the car is in LINE\_LOST and actively doing an arc search to find the line again (REACQUIRING\_TRACK), this is the deadline. If 2 seconds pass with no line found, the car gives up entirely and reports TRACK\_LOST up to the Vehicle Controller, which then stops the car completely.  |
| D\_cmd | 30 cm | Barcode: pending command expires if no junction is reached Once the car decodes a valid barcode ("turn left"), that command sits pending until the car physically reaches a junction. D\_cmd is a distance limit, not a time limit, if the car travels 30cm without hitting a junction, the pending command is thrown away. This stops a barcode read early on a straight stretch from firing on some unrelated junction way down the track. |
| T\_end | 3 × widest element time | Barcode: end-of-symbol quiet gap Code 39 barcodes are made of bars and gaps. This is how the decoder knows the barcode is finished, if the gap between bars is 3 times longer than the widest bar/space it's seen so far, that's read as "end of symbol," not just a wide gap. |
| D\_detect | 25 cm | Obstacle Scanning: triggers fine scan If the coarse sweep sees something closer than 25cm, twice in a row, that's the trigger to stop coarse-sweeping and switch to a slower, narrower "fine scan" to pin down exactly where the obstacle's edges are. |
| Side clearance margin | 5 cm | Bypass decision: clearance \> car width \+ margin Once the fine scan measures how much open space is on the left vs. right of the obstacle, the car only picks a side if that gap is bigger than the car's own width plus this 5cm safety buffer. Without the margin, the car might attempt a bypass gap that's technically wide enough but leaves zero room for error. |
| Bypass budget | 3.0 s | Obstacle Avoidance (NFR14); worst case 3.0 s \+ T\_search \= 5.0 s Once the car commits to going around an obstacle, this is the target time to finish the whole maneuver (leave the line, pass the obstacle, come back). It's a performance target for grading, not a hard cutoff. |
| T\_hold | 100 ms | Motion Control holds its last setpoint, then stops Motion Control expects a fresh command roughly every 20ms. If nothing new arrives (for example, in the split-second handoff between Obstacle Avoidance finishing and Line-Following resuming), Motion Control keeps doing whatever it was last told to do for up to 100ms rather than immediately stopping or going blank. It's a buffer against a one-tick gap in commands causing a visible stutter. |
| a\_move | 0.05 g | IMU: motion start The acceleration threshold that means "the car has started moving." Below this, the IMU task treats the car as STATIONARY and uses that quiet time to re-check its own gyroscope's zero-point (bias). |
| degree\_hump | 5° | IMU: hump entry If the car's pitch (nose tilting up or down) exceeds 5 degrees while moving, combined with a vertical acceleration spike, that's read as "the car is going over a hump," not just normal driving vibration. |
| g\_collision | 2.5 g | IMU: collision spike The acceleration spike threshold for "this was a crash, not a bump." Anything above 2.5g in any moving state immediately triggers the collision fault, no matter what else the car is doing. |
| T\_still | 500 ms | “Stationary” for reset: encoder speed zero for T\_still Before the car will accept a reset command after a collision fault, the encoders must read zero speed continuously for 500ms. This exists so a reset can't be sent while the car is still physically moving or sliding, which could restart the motors dangerously. |
| T\_ka / backoff | 5 s keep-alive; 1–30 s backoff | Telemetry reconnection (FR3) If the MQTT broker doesn't respond to a keep-alive check within 5 seconds, the connection is considered dead and the car tries to reconnect. Each failed retry waits longer than the last (1s, then 2s, then 4s...) up to a 30s cap, so a dead network doesn't get hammered with constant retry attempts. |

## **3.3 Inter-Task Communication Objects and Queue Policies**

| Object | Type / depth | Senders, receiver and timeouts |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| MBF\_NAV\_IN | Message buffer, 8 × nav\_input\_t Steering, barcode, and obstacle commands, all addressed to the Vehicle Controller | Line-Following sends with TMO\_POL (a dropped steering update is replaced 20 ms later). Barcode Decode, Obstacle Avoidance and Telemetry send with a 5 ms timeout and log an error if it expires. The Vehicle Controller receives with TMO\_FEVR; because it runs at P2 and drains the buffer at once, a remote STOP waits behind at most a few messages. Holds 8 messages. Line-Following's steering updates use a "don't wait, just drop it" policy (TMO\_POL) because a missed steering update gets replaced 20ms later anyway, no harm done. Barcode and Obstacle Avoidance instead wait up to 5ms and log an error if the mailbox is full, because those commands are one-off and important, silently dropping a turn command would be worse than silently dropping one steering tick. |
| MBF\_MOTION\_CMD | Message buffer, 4 × motion\_cmd\_t The one resolved command Motion Control actually executes | Vehicle Controller sends with TMO\_POL. Motion Control polls with TMO\_POL every 20 ms tick and holds its last setpoint for up to T\_hold if no command arrives. Only 4 slots, because Motion Control checks it fresh every 20ms tick, it never needs a backlog.  |
| MBF\_OBSTACLE | Message buffer, 2 × obstacle\_profile\_t The obstacle's location/width/clearance | Obstacle Scanning sends with TMO\_POL (newest profile wins); Obstacle Avoidance receives with TMO\_FEVR. Only 2 slots, newest reading always wins. An old obstacle measurement is worthless the moment a new one arrives. |
| MBF\_TELEMETRY | Message buffer, 32 × tel\_evt\_t Status and sensor events on their way to the dashboard | All producers send with TMO\_POL; overflows are counted, never waited on (NFR1). Telemetry receives with a 200 ms timeout. 32 slots, generous because telemetry is the lowest priority and least urgent, but if it does fill up, messages are dropped and counted rather than making any task wait (this is the NFR1 rule you saw earlier, "never block a control task for the network's sake"). |
| Barcode edge ring | ISR ring buffer, 64 edges Raw timestamp of every bar/space edge the barcode sensor sees | Written by the GP28 ISR; read by Barcode Decode after tk\_wup\_tsk. Overflow forces INVALID\_READ\_RESET. Not a real IPC object, it's a simple buffer the interrupt writes into directly. 64 slots because one full barcode symbol only needs 29 edges, so there's headroom. |
| SEM\_ECHO | Semaphore | Signalled by the echo ISR; Obstacle Scanning waits with a 30 ms timeout (no echo \= nothing in range). A semaphore doesn't carry data, it's a doorbell. Obstacle Scanning waits up to 30ms for the doorbell; if nothing arrives, it assumes "no obstacle in range" rather than waiting forever. |
| EVF\_SAFETY | Eventflag: COLLISION, IMU\_ALIVE, FAULT\_LATCHED | IMU Processing sets COLLISION and IMU\_ALIVE. Only Safety sets FAULT\_LATCHED; only the Vehicle Controller clears it, on car/cmd/reset while stationary. Grouping these as flags (rather than three separate objects) lets Safety wait on "either one changing" in a single call. |
| EVF\_NAV | Eventflag: AVOID\_ACTIVE, LINE\_FOUND, LINE\_REACQUIRED | Obstacle Avoidance sets AVOID\_ACTIVE and LINE\_REACQUIRED; Line-Following sets LINE\_FOUND. Readers poll with TMO\_POL and never block on it. These are status flags different tasks check by polling (never blocking), because none of them are urgent enough to justify a task sitting around waiting. |
| MTX\_MOTION | Mutex, TA\_INHERIT (priority inheritance) A lock protecting the shared motion\_state\_t struct (speed, distance, encoder counts) | Guards motion\_state\_t. Motion Control writes; Barcode Decode and Telemetry copy the struct and release at once. Safety never takes it. Uses "priority inheritance" (TA\_INHERIT), meaning if a low-priority task is holding the lock and a high-priority task needs it, the low-priority task temporarily gets boosted so it finishes fast and hands the lock over instead of blocking the important task indefinitely. Safety deliberately never touches this lock at all, so a stuck lock can never delay an emergency stop. |
| enc\_count\[2\] | Volatile counters Raw pulse counts from both wheel encoders | Written by the encoder ISR; Motion Control reads and clears both inside a short interrupt-disabled section. Not a kernel object either, just two numbers the interrupt increments. Motion Control briefly disables interrupts to read and reset them safely, since you can't "lock" something an ISR might change mid-read any other way. |

# **4\. Task Interaction Diagram**

Show RTOS tasks, queues, semaphores, mutexes, event groups, notifications, and data flow. Clearly distinguish software tasks from hardware devices and interrupt service routines.

## 

| ![][image1] |
| :---- |

Brief explanation of the main communication paths:

| All navigation decisions go through one arbitration point. Line-Following (P4), Barcode Decode (P5) and Obstacle Avoidance (P7) never drive the motors themselves. Each posts a tagged message (nav\_input\_t) into the Nav Input Queue (MBF\_NAV\_IN), and the Vehicle Controller (P2) is its only reader. The Vehicle Controller resolves conflicts in a fixed order (Safety › Avoidance › Barcode › Line), tracks which subsystem currently has authority (LINE or AVOID), and sends exactly one command through the Motion Cmd Queue to Motion Control (P3). Motion Control is the only task that drives motor PWM on GP8–GP11. The single exception is the Safety task’s emergency stop, which calls one motion-library function, motion\_emergency\_brake(), to set all four channels LOW (brake) inside a critical section; after that, FAULT\_LATCHED blocks every other PWM write. Remote start, stop and reset commands parsed by the Telemetry task enter the same queue, so the operator has no side channel to the motors. Queue depths and timeouts are listed in Section 3.3. Hardware reaches the tasks in two ways. Time-critical signals are captured by interrupt routines: encoder pulses (GP6/GP7), barcode edges timestamped in microseconds (GP28), and ultrasonic echo width (GP5). Each routine does the minimum work and hands off to its task through a counter, a ring buffer with a task wake-up, or a semaphore. The IMU and track IR sensors are polled inside their periodic tasks. The safety path is kept separate from normal data flow: IMU Processing sets EVF\_SAFETY.COLLISION on a g-spike and refreshes IMU\_ALIVE on every sample, and the P1 Safety task brakes if the collision flag is set or the heartbeat stops for 50 ms. Status and fault events flow to the Telemetry task (P9) through a status queue that drops messages when full, so network problems can never block a control task. Motion Control publishes speed and distance in motion\_state\_t, guarded by a priority-inheritance mutex; Barcode Decode reads it for speed-normalised decoding and Telemetry for reporting, and the Safety task never takes it. |
| :---- |

# 

# **5\. System-Level Statechart**

Model the operating states of the entire system. Label transition events or conditions. Include relevant fault, stop, or recovery behaviour.

## 

| ![][image2] |
| :---- |

Explain the main states and any important assumptions:

| The vehicle powers up into INITIALISING, where it calibrates the IMU bias and IR baselines, checks the encoders and attempts a WiFi/MQTT connection. A passed self-test moves it to READY – WAITING FOR START with the motors stopped. A failed self-test goes straight to the fault state. car/cmd/start enters AUTONOMOUS NAVIGATION. There, the car tracks the line, slows through humps, and branches at junctions according to a validated barcode: A turns left, B turns right, C goes straight and D makes a u-turn. A confirmed obstacle moves the car into OBSTACLE AVOIDANCE / BYPASS, which suspends line-following. The only way back to navigation is a LINE\_REACQUIRED handoff. If Line-Following cannot find the line afterwards (TRACK\_LOST after T\_search), or the operator sends car/cmd/stop, the car stops and returns to READY. A collision g-spike, or a 50 ms loss of IMU data, in any moving state enters SAFETY – COLLISION LATCHED FAULT. The motors are braked and all motion is inhibited until car/cmd/reset arrives while the car is stationary (encoder speed zero for T\_still). The chart assumes that loss of WiFi only degrades telemetry and never changes vehicle state; the team accepts that the car cannot be stopped remotely while the link is down (Section 8.3). It also assumes that power-off is possible from any state, and that the only barcode commands are Left, Right and Straight and U-turn. |
| :---- |

# 

# **6\. Subsystem Statecharts**

## **6.1 Subsystem Statechart 1**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | Navigation / Line-Following Controller |
| Related RTOS task(s) | Line-Following Control, Motion Control |
| Purpose | Track ON\_LINE → JUNCTION\_DETECTED → LINE\_LOST → REACQUIRING\_TRACK, plus SUSPENDED\_BY\_AVOIDANCE during a bypass, and drive corrective steering |
| Reason a statechart is needed | Track loss vs. junction vs. reacquisition require different control laws; ambiguity here causes wrong turns or erratic steering |

| ![][image3] |
| :---: |

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| In ON\_LINE, the task samples IR\_L and IR\_C every 5 ms, computes the line error against the calibrated baseline and posts a steering correction every 20 ms. When both sensors read dark for N consecutive samples, it enters JUNCTION\_DETECTED and executes the pending barcode command; if none is pending, it goes straight. A u-turn pivots the car 180° in place, and the line then has T\_uturn rather than T\_turn to reappear. A pending command expires if no junction is reached within D\_cmd, so a stray barcode cannot trigger a turn at a later junction. When both sensors read light for longer than T\_lost, or no line appears within T\_turn after a turn, the task enters LINE\_LOST, stops, and records which side the line was last seen on. REACQUIRING\_TRACK then performs an arc search towards that side and returns to ON\_LINE (setting LINE\_FOUND) when the center sensor detects the line again. During obstacle avoidance the task sits in SUSPENDED\_BY\_AVOIDANCE. It keeps sampling and still sets LINE\_FOUND, which Obstacle Avoidance uses to finish the bypass, but it posts no steering. It resumes on LINE\_REACQUIRED once the Vehicle Controller has switched authority back to LINE, or starts its own search if the handoff arrives without the line found. Fault handling: N-sample hysteresis on both thresholds prevents rapid state switching from noise. If the search exceeds T\_search, the task reports TRACK\_LOST to the Vehicle Controller, which stops the car. With only two line sensors, a junction cannot be told apart from a wide dark patch; this is accepted as a risk and checked during track testing. |
| :---- |

## 

## **6.2 Subsystem Statechart 2**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | Barcode Decoder |
| Related RTOS task(s) | Barcode Decode |
| Purpose | Track IDLE → EDGE\_CAPTURE\_READING → VALIDATING\_CHECKSUM → COMMAND\_READY / INVALID\_READ\_RESET |
| Reason a statechart is needed | Edge-capture and checksum validation is multi-step; an incomplete or invalid read must not be issued as a navigation command |

| ![][image4] |
| :---: |

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| The decoder waits in IDLE until the barcode edge interrupt timestamps the first bar on GP28. In EDGE\_CAPTURE\_READING, each edge is converted to a physical width by multiplying the time between edges by the current wheel velocity, copied from motion\_state\_t under its mutex. Once a quiet gap longer than T\_end is seen and the expected element count is reached, the read moves to VALIDATING\_CHECKSUM. Each Code 39 character is classified narrow or wide by its ratio to the median element width, so changes in speed cancel out. Validation checks the start and stop characters, the 3-of-9 wide-element pattern and, if the track symbols carry one, the mod-43 check character. It also requires the decoded character to be A, B, C or D. A valid read enters COMMAND\_READY, posts the mapped command (Left, Right, Straight or U turn) to the Nav Input Queue, and ignores repeats of the same code for a short distance. The command stays pending until the next junction, or expires after D\_cmd. Any failure leads to INVALID\_READ\_RESET. Failures include edge-buffer overflow, the vehicle stalling mid-read, a capture timeout, a structural or ratio error, or a character outside A–D. The reset flushes the edge buffer, logs INVALID\_READ to telemetry and returns to IDLE. An incomplete or invalid read is therefore never issued as a navigation command. |
| :---- |

## 

## **6.3 Subsystem Statechart 3**

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | Obstacle Avoidance / Ultrasonic Scanning |
| Related RTOS task(s) | Obstacle Scanning, Obstacle Avoidance & Recovery |
| Purpose | Track SWEEPING\_COARSE → FINE\_SCAN\_LOCALIZATION → BYPASS\_DECISION → EXECUTING\_BYPASS → LINE\_REACQUIRED\_HANDOFF, with BLOCKED\_STOP when no side is clear |
| Reason a statechart is needed | Scanning/decision behavior changes with detection state, and must hand off cleanly to line-following (FR13) |

| ![][image5] |
| :---: |

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| In SWEEPING\_COARSE, the servo steps across a wide arc and each range is the median of three pings, which rejects outlier echoes (NFR13). Two consecutive readings below D\_detect move the task to FINE\_SCAN\_LOCALIZATION and ask the Vehicle Controller to slow down. A narrow sweep then finds the obstacle’s edges. If the hit is not confirmed, the task returns to coarse sweeping. In BYPASS\_DECISION, the task estimates obstacle width W and the clearances dL and dR, then picks the side with clearance greater than the car’s width plus a margin. It sets AVOID\_ACTIVE and enters EXECUTING\_BYPASS, which runs LEAVE\_LINE, PASS\_OBSTACLE and RETURN\_TO\_LINE in sequence. When Line-Following reports LINE\_FOUND (it owns the center IR sensor), the task enters LINE\_REACQUIRED\_HANDOFF. It posts a RELEASE message to the Vehicle Controller, sets LINE\_REACQUIRED and clears AVOID\_ACTIVE. On RELEASE, the Vehicle Controller switches authority to LINE and discards any AVOID message queued after it, so a stale bypass command can never run after the handoff. Between the last bypass command and the first steering update, Motion Control holds its last setpoint for up to T\_hold, so no control frame is left undefined. This handoff is the single mandatory exit, so the two tasks never drive the motors together. Fault handling: if neither side is clear, the task enters BLOCKED\_STOP, stopping or reversing until the path clears. If the bypass exceeds its 3.0 s budget, the handoff still happens with “line not found” and Line-Following starts its own search, limited by T\_search, so the worst case from obstacle to TRACK\_LOST stop is 5.0 s. A collision in any state is handled by the system-level safety latch. |
| :---- |

## 

## **6.4 Subsystem Statechart 4** {#6.4-subsystem-statechart-4}

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | IMU / Terrain & Safety Monitor |
| Related RTOS task(s) | IMU Processing, Safety/Collision Response |
| Purpose | Track STATIONARY → ACCELERATING → CRUISING ⇄ TURNING, HUMP\_DETECTED from any moving state, and a latched COLLISION\_FAULT |
| Reason a statechart is needed | Motion classification and safety response depend on current dynamic state; a Fault state must latch until reset to avoid unsafe continued driving |

| ![][image6] |
| :---: |

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| IMU Processing samples every 10 ms, estimates pitch and roll with a complementary filter, and refreshes the IMU\_ALIVE heartbeat on every sample. It classifies motion as STATIONARY (used to re-estimate gyro bias), ACCELERATING, CRUISING or TURNING, based on longitudinal acceleration and gyro turn rate. From any moving state, a pitch above θ\_hump together with a vertical acceleration spike enters HUMP\_DETECTED. Hump height is computed as the sum of sin(pitch) × encoder distance across the hump, which avoids the drift of double-integrated acceleration; h ≈ v²/2g from the vertical impulse is kept as a cross-check. When pitch settles, the peak is logged and the highest hump of the run is reported (FR11). A total acceleration above g\_collision in any moving state enters COLLISION\_FAULT and sets EVF\_SAFETY.COLLISION. The P1 Safety task then calls motion\_emergency\_brake() and sets FAULT\_LATCHED; Safety is the only task that sets the latch, and the Vehicle Controller is the only task that clears it. The fault is latched: every event except car/cmd/reset while stationary (encoder speed zero for T\_still) is ignored, so the car cannot drive on after an impact. If IMU Processing itself stalls (for example, an I2C bus hang), IMU\_ALIVE stops updating and Safety stops the car after 50 ms. Initial values for a\_move, θ\_hump and g\_collision are in Section 3.2 and will be tuned from logged runs (A4). |
| :---- |

## 

## **6.5 Subsystem Statechart 5** {#6.5-subsystem-statechart-5}

| Field | Student Entry |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subsystem name | WiFi / MQTT Connectivity |
| Related RTOS task(s) | Telemetry / MQTT (connection monitoring runs inside this task) |
| Purpose | Track DISCONNECTED → CONNECTING → CONNECTED → DEGRADED\_BUFFERING → RECONNECTING |
| Reason a statechart is needed | Network state determines whether telemetry is live, buffered, or dropped, and governs backoff without stalling the main loop |

| ![][image7] |
| :---: |

Brief explanation of states, events, and fault handling:

| The Telemetry task starts in DISCONNECTED and, once system initialisation completes, begins an asynchronous WiFi join and MQTT CONNECT in CONNECTING. On a successful join and CONNACK, it enters CONNECTED. It subscribes to car/cmd/\#, publishes telemetry every 200 ms and sends a heartbeat every second. If a publish fails or the broker misses a keep-alive response, the task enters DEGRADED\_BUFFERING. New telemetry is stored in a ring buffer; when the buffer is full, the oldest message is dropped and counted. If the link recovers, the buffer is flushed and the task returns to CONNECTED. If the keep-alive timeout T\_ka expires, it moves to RECONNECTING. A join or CONNACK timeout also leads to RECONNECTING. RECONNECTING retries with exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s … up to 30 s) and returns to CONNECTING when the timer expires. Connection monitoring (heartbeat, keep-alive and backoff) is part of this task rather than a separate one. All network I/O, including every lwIP call, runs inside the P9 task, so the network stack is never used from two threads (A9). Other tasks post to the status queue without waiting and drop messages if it is full. A network failure therefore never stalls a control task (NFR1, A3), and link state never changes vehicle behaviour. |
| :---- |

# **9\. Design Consistency**

Use this section to demonstrate that the design artefacts describe one coherent system rather than independent diagrams.

| Check | Student Response |
| :---- | :---- |
| Which task owns each hardware device? | Each hardware device has one owning task. Buddy 2’s Motion Control task owns the drive motors (GP8–GP11) and wheel encoders (GP6/GP7); the Safety task can only call the motion library’s emergency-brake function. Buddy 3’s Line-Following task owns the track IR sensors (GP26/GP27) and the Barcode Decode task owns the barcode IR sensor (GP28). Buddy 4’s IMU Processing task owns the IMU (I2C on GP2/GP3). Buddy 5’s Obstacle Scanning task owns the ultrasonic sensor (GP4/GP5) and the servo (GP12). Buddy 1’s Telemetry / MQTT task owns the onboard WiFi module, including connection monitoring. |
| Which task has the highest priority, and why? | The Safety / Collision Response task (P1). A detected collision must override every navigation command and brake the motors immediately. Because collision detection itself runs in the P8 IMU task, Safety also enforces a 50 ms IMU watchdog, so a starved or stalled detector still results in a stop. |
| Which subsystem statechart corresponds to which RTOS task or subsystem? | Statechart 6.1 (Navigation / Line-Following) maps to Line-Following Control, with Motion Control executing its steering. 6.2 (Barcode Decoder) maps to Barcode Decode. 6.3 (Obstacle Avoidance) maps to Obstacle Scanning and Obstacle Avoidance & Recovery. 6.4 (IMU / Terrain & Safety) maps to IMU Processing and Safety / Collision Response. 6.5 (WiFi / MQTT) maps to Telemetry / MQTT, which also performs connection monitoring. The system-level statechart (Section 5\) is held by the Vehicle Controller. |
| How are functional requirements reflected in the task and statechart design? | Telemetry, remote commands and network recovery (FR1–FR3) are handled by the Telemetry / MQTT task and statechart 6.5. Motion functions, straight-line PID correction and speed/distance estimation (FR4–FR6) are handled by Motion Control. Barcode decoding at varying speeds and command mapping (FR7, FR9) are handled by Barcode Decode and statechart 6.2. Line following and track-loss recovery (FR8, FR10) are handled by Line-Following and statechart 6.1. Hump detection (FR11) is handled by IMU Processing, and the collision stop (FR12) by IMU Processing with the Safety task, both in statechart 6.4. The avoidance-to-line handoff (FR13) links statecharts 6.3 and 6.1, and two-stage obstacle scanning (FR14) is handled by Obstacle Scanning and statechart 6.3. |
| What changes are still expected after the Week 6 review? | Expected changes include empirical tuning of the PID constants, the Section 3.2 thresholds (hump, collision, junction and obstacle distances) and the ultrasonic sweep timing, based on measured execution latency during Tribunal 1 integration testing. Assumptions A1–A11 will be closed with recorded test evidence, and the Pico C SDK and CMake configuration may change as interrupt priorities are finalized. |
